report_metadata.sdlc_rationale: Requirements fully defined and signed off with fixed deadline and budget, but stakeholder validation of new portal UX and integration workflows with Workday/Azure AD necessitates working software in Phase 2–3 before final launch.

project_understanding.primary_goal: Build a self-service employee onboarding portal enabling new hires to complete required paperwork, set up IT accounts, and receive team introductions before day one.
project_understanding.beneficiary: New employees (100–200/year) and HR team (5 people)
project_understanding.trigger: Current onboarding is fragmented across PDF-based paperwork, manual IT account setup, and unstructured team introductions; new hires report feeling unprepared on day one; CEO escalated after hearing complaints at all-hands.
success_definition: 80% of onboarding tasks completed by new hires before day one
IT account setup fully automated (zero manual tickets)
supporting_quotes: Create a self-service employee onboarding portal that allows new hires to complete all required paperwork, set up their IT accounts, and get introduced to the team before day one.
Currently onboarding is fragmented - paperwork is PDF-based, IT account setup is manual, new hires feel unprepared on day one.
CEO asked HR to fix this after hearing complaints at all-hands.

New hires can complete 80% of onboarding tasks before day one; HR time spent on onboarding admin reduced by 50%; IT account setup automated (no manual tickets); New hire satisfaction survey score > 4/5

assumption_log.what: Workday API sandbox environment, documentation, and SLA are available and stable; integration does not require custom Workday development or extended vendor support.
assumption_log.why: External API integrations are a common source of schedule risk on internal projects. Assuming standard API availability and documentation is reasonable for a major HRIS vendor, but must be validated before Phase 2 begins.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 8.1 (Scope Management) and Section 12.1 (Integration Management); risk of external dependency blocking development.
assumption_log.consequence: If Workday API is unavailable, undocumented, or requires custom development, Phase 2 integration work will slip by 2–4 weeks, compressing Phase 3 testing and risking June 30 deadline.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Enables Phase 2 to proceed without Workday vendor engagement delay. Risks: If API is unavailable or requires custom work, schedule slips and contingency budget is consumed.

assumption_log.what: Azure AD SSO integration is standard OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect; team has prior experience with Azure AD or equivalent SSO implementation.
assumption_log.why: Input specifies Azure AD stack but does not state team experience level. For a 4-person team on a 4-month deadline, assuming competence with the named stack is standard practice unless input flags inexperience.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 9.1 (Resource Management); assumes team capability matches stated technology stack.
assumption_log.consequence: If team lacks Azure AD experience and must learn during Phase 2, authentication implementation will slip 1–2 weeks, consuming contingency and risking Phase 3 timeline.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Enables Phase 2 to proceed without pre-project training or external contractor. Risks: If team is unfamiliar with Azure AD, ramp-up time compresses testing window.

assumption_log.what: SOC 2 Type II compliance scope is limited to data handling, audit logging, and access controls within the portal; does not require third-party audit, penetration testing, or infrastructure re-architecture beyond standard Azure App Service security practices.
assumption_log.why: Input names SOC 2 as a requirement but does not specify scope (Type I vs. Type II, audit timeline, third-party assessor involvement). For internal software, assuming standard data protection and audit logging is reasonable; full third-party audit would typically be called out explicitly.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 (Scope Definition); compliance scope must be explicit to avoid scope creep.
assumption_log.consequence: If SOC 2 Type II audit is required before launch (vs. post-launch), Phase 3 will require 4–8 weeks of audit preparation, evidence collection, and remediation, pushing launch past June 30 deadline.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Enables Phase 3 to focus on functional testing and launch readiness. Risks: If full SOC 2 audit is required pre-launch, schedule slips and budget is consumed by audit and remediation work.

assumption_log.what: E-signature service (DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or equivalent) is already contracted or available for integration; API documentation and sandbox are accessible; no additional procurement or vendor negotiation required.
assumption_log.why: Input lists e-signature as a must-have feature and mentions 'integrated e-signature service' in use cases, but does not name the vendor or confirm procurement status. Assuming a standard SaaS e-signature service is available is reasonable for a company of this size, but vendor selection and contract terms are not stated.
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 12.1 (Integration Management); external service availability is a critical dependency.
assumption_log.consequence: If e-signature vendor is not yet selected or contracted, procurement and vendor onboarding will consume 2–3 weeks in Phase 1, compressing Phase 2 development window.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Enables Phase 2 to begin e-signature integration immediately. Risks: If vendor is not yet selected, Phase 1 extends and Phase 2 start date slips.

assumption_log.what: Data retention policy for onboarding documents (I-9, W-4, direct deposit forms) is 7 years (standard IRS/employment law requirement); no extended retention or archival to separate cold storage is required.
assumption_log.why: Input does not specify data retention requirements. For employment documents, 7-year retention is the standard IRS requirement; assuming this default is reasonable unless input specifies longer retention or compliance with additional regulations (e.g., state-specific requirements).
assumption_log.pmi_basis: PMBOK 6th Ed, Section 5.2 (Scope Definition); data retention affects storage architecture and compliance scope.
assumption_log.consequence: If retention requirement is longer than 7 years or includes state-specific rules, database schema and archival strategy must be redesigned in Phase 2, consuming 1–2 weeks of development time.
assumption_log.tradeoff: Gains: Enables Phase 2 to use standard PostgreSQL retention and backup strategy. Risks: If retention is longer or more complex, storage and compliance architecture must be redesigned.

hard.technology_stack: Frontend: React + TypeScript; Backend: Node.js + PostgreSQL; Integration: Workday API, Azure AD SSO; Hosting: Azure App Service
hard.compliance: SOC 2 compliance required (data handling, audit logs)

nfr.security: Azure AD SSO authentication; SOC 2 compliance (audit logging, data handling, access controls)

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Is SOC 2 Type II audit required before launch (June 30, 2026), or is Type II audit acceptable post-launch with Type I compliance at launch?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If Type II audit is required pre-launch, Phase 3 must include 4–8 weeks of audit preparation and evidence collection, pushing launch past deadline. If post-launch is acceptable, Phase 3 focuses on functional testing and launch readiness.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Has the e-signature service vendor been selected and contracted? If not, who owns vendor selection and procurement in Phase 1?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If vendor is not yet selected, Phase 1 procurement will consume 2–3 weeks, compressing Phase 2 development window and risking June 30 deadline.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Who is the Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization, sprint planning, and stakeholder feedback during Phase 2–3 sprints?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires a dedicated PO to manage backlog and sprint cycles. Without clear PO assignment, sprint planning will stall and stakeholder feedback loops will be delayed.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: What is the data retention requirement for onboarding documents (I-9, W-4, direct deposit forms)? Is 7-year IRS standard sufficient, or are there state-specific or company-specific retention policies?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If retention requirement exceeds 7 years or includes state-specific rules, database schema and archival strategy must be redesigned in Phase 2, consuming 1–2 weeks of development time.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: Is Workday API sandbox environment, documentation, and SLA confirmed available? Does integration require custom Workday development or extended vendor support?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: If Workday API is unavailable, undocumented, or requires custom development, Phase 2 integration work will slip 2–4 weeks, compressing Phase 3 testing and risking June 30 deadline.

open_questions_pre_planning.question: What is the definition of 'IT account setup automated'? Does this include provisioning in Slack, SaaS tools (which ones?), and email, or is email provisioning sufficient for MVP?
open_questions_pre_planning.impact_if_unanswered: Scope of IT account provisioning affects Phase 2 integration complexity and Phase 3 testing scope. Unclear scope may result in feature creep or incomplete automation at launch.

critical_path_summary.staffing_implication: Backend Developer and Frontend Developer must be dedicated (not shared) across Phases 2–4 due to critical path dependency; PM and UX Designer front-loaded in Phase 1 with reduced allocation in Phases 2–3.

risk_register.description: If SOC 2 Type II audit is required before June 30, 2026 launch (vs. post-launch), then Phase 3 will require 4–8 weeks of audit preparation, evidence collection, and remediation, pushing launch past the fixed deadline and consuming contingency budget.
risk_register.trigger: Stakeholder clarifies that SOC 2 Type II audit must be completed and passed before launch, not post-launch
risk_register.mitigation: Obtain written clarification from compliance/legal stakeholder before Phase 2 begins on whether Type II audit is pre-launch or post-launch; if pre-launch, allocate 4–8 weeks in Phase 3 schedule and budget for audit preparation and evidence collection
risk_register.contingency: If audit scope is confirmed as pre-launch during Phase 2, immediately compress Phase 3 functional testing window and defer non-critical features to post-launch; engage SOC 2 auditor by week 16 to begin evidence collection in parallel with development

risk_register.description: If Workday API sandbox environment is unavailable, undocumented, or requires custom development not covered by standard vendor support, then Phase 2 integration work will slip 2–4 weeks, compressing Phase 3 testing window and risking June 30 deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 begins and Workday API sandbox is not accessible, documentation is incomplete, or vendor indicates custom development is required
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 kickoff, validate Workday API sandbox access, review API documentation completeness, and confirm with Workday vendor that standard OAuth/REST integration is supported without custom development; document SLA and support contact
risk_register.contingency: If Workday API is unavailable or requires custom work, immediately escalate to Workday account manager for expedited support; identify alternative data import method (e.g., CSV upload, manual data entry) as fallback for Phase 2; compress Phase 3 testing by deferring non-critical Workday integrations to post-launch

risk_register.description: If e-signature service vendor has not been selected and contracted before Phase 1 ends, then vendor procurement and onboarding will consume 2–3 weeks in Phase 1, compressing Phase 2 development window and delaying UC2 (Submit Required Documents) implementation.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 week 2 and e-signature vendor is not yet selected, contract not signed, or API documentation not available
risk_register.mitigation: Assign vendor selection and procurement ownership in Phase 1 kickoff (PM or Procurement); evaluate DocuSign, Adobe Sign, and equivalent services against integration requirements and cost; complete vendor selection and contract signature by Phase 1 week 2; request API sandbox access and documentation immediately upon contract signature
risk_register.contingency: If vendor selection slips past Phase 1 week 2, defer e-signature integration to Phase 2 sprint 2 and implement manual document upload + HR review as interim solution for Phase 2 sprint 1; prioritize e-signature API integration in Phase 2 sprint 2 to unblock UC2 testing

risk_register.description: If Backend Developer or Frontend Developer is pulled off project for competing priorities or becomes unavailable, then critical path tasks (T1, T3, T5, T8, T12, T16, T20, T24, T28, T31) will slip, compressing Phase 3 and risking June 30 deadline; team size of 4 with 2 developers leaves no backup capacity.
risk_register.trigger: Either Backend Developer or Frontend Developer is reassigned to another project, takes unplanned leave, or is unavailable for >1 week during Phases 2–4
risk_register.mitigation: Secure written commitment from development manager that both Backend Developer and Frontend Developer are 100% allocated to this project for full 26-week duration with no competing priorities; document in project charter; establish weekly check-in with dev manager to confirm allocation status
risk_register.contingency: If either developer becomes unavailable, immediately escalate to development manager and project sponsor for resource replacement; identify and onboard backup developer from same team within 1 week; compress Phase 2 scope by deferring non-critical features (e.g., chat with HR bot, mobile app) to post-launch

risk_register.description: If team lacks prior experience with Azure AD SSO (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect), then authentication implementation in Phase 2 will require 1–2 weeks of learning and ramp-up, consuming contingency and compressing Phase 3 testing window.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint 1 begins and Backend Developer or Frontend Developer indicates unfamiliarity with Azure AD or OAuth 2.0 implementation patterns
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 kickoff, confirm team experience with Azure AD and OAuth 2.0 in pre-project assessment; if experience is limited, allocate 3–5 days in Phase 1 for team training on Azure AD SSO patterns and sandbox testing; document team capability in project charter
risk_register.contingency: If team lacks Azure AD experience during Phase 2, allocate 1–2 weeks for guided learning and proof-of-concept; engage Azure AD specialist or contractor for 1–2 weeks to accelerate implementation; defer non-critical authentication features (e.g., multi-factor authentication) to post-launch

risk_register.description: If Product Owner is not assigned or is unavailable for timely backlog prioritization and stakeholder feedback during Phase 2–3 sprints, then sprint planning will stall, stakeholder feedback loops will be delayed, and Phase 3 testing will be compressed.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint 1 planning begins and Product Owner is not identified, or PO is allocated <50% to project and unavailable for sprint ceremonies
risk_register.mitigation: Assign dedicated Product Owner before Phase 1 ends; confirm PO is allocated ≥50% to project for full 26-week duration; document PO responsibilities in project charter (backlog prioritization, sprint planning, stakeholder feedback, acceptance criteria definition); schedule weekly PO sync with PM and development team
risk_register.contingency: If PO becomes unavailable during Phase 2–3, immediately escalate to project sponsor and identify backup PO from business stakeholder team; establish daily standup with backup PO to maintain sprint momentum; defer non-critical features to post-launch to reduce backlog prioritization burden

risk_register.description: If IT account provisioning scope is not clearly defined (email only vs. email + Slack + SaaS tools), then Phase 2 integration complexity will be underestimated, Phase 3 testing scope will be unclear, and UC4 (Provision IT Accounts) may be incomplete at launch.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 requirements review and stakeholders cannot agree on which systems must be auto-provisioned (email, Slack, SaaS tools) vs. manual setup
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 begins, obtain written definition of 'IT account setup automated' from IT Administrator and HR stakeholder; list specific systems (email, Slack, SaaS tools) that must be auto-provisioned; define MVP scope (e.g., email + Slack) vs. post-launch scope (e.g., additional SaaS tools); document in requirements traceability matrix
risk_register.contingency: If scope is unclear during Phase 2, implement email provisioning as MVP in Phase 2 sprint 1; defer Slack and SaaS tool provisioning to Phase 2 sprint 2 or Phase 3 based on stakeholder priority; use feature flags to enable/disable provisioning integrations at launch

risk_register.description: If data retention requirement for onboarding documents exceeds 7-year IRS standard or includes state-specific rules, then database schema and archival strategy must be redesigned in Phase 2, consuming 1–2 weeks of development time and compressing Phase 3.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 requirements review and HR/Legal stakeholder specifies retention requirement >7 years or state-specific retention rules (e.g., California, New York)
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 begins, obtain written data retention policy from HR and Legal stakeholders; confirm 7-year IRS standard is sufficient or identify any state-specific or company-specific retention rules; document in non-functional requirements; design database schema and archival strategy in Phase 1 to accommodate confirmed retention policy
risk_register.contingency: If retention requirement is longer than 7 years or includes state-specific rules, implement tiered storage strategy (hot storage for <7 years, cold storage for 7+ years) in Phase 2; defer advanced archival features (e.g., encryption key rotation, compliance reporting) to post-launch

risk_register.description: If external e-signature service API is rate-limited or has availability SLA <99.5%, then high-volume document signing during peak onboarding periods may fail or be delayed, affecting UC2 (Submit Required Documents) and UC8 (Collect E-signatures).
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 integration testing and e-signature service experiences rate limiting, downtime, or SLA breach during load testing
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 integration begins, review e-signature vendor SLA and rate limits; confirm SLA ≥99.5% uptime and rate limits support expected peak load (e.g., 50 concurrent signings); implement request queuing and retry logic in Phase 2 to handle rate limiting gracefully; design fallback to manual document upload if e-signature service is unavailable
risk_register.contingency: If e-signature service is unavailable or rate-limited during Phase 3 testing, implement manual document upload + HR review as fallback; queue signing requests and retry with exponential backoff; escalate to e-signature vendor for SLA breach investigation and remediation

risk_register.description: If Azure AD tenant configuration, group policies, or security settings are not aligned with portal requirements, then SSO integration (UC7) may fail or require security policy changes that delay Phase 2 implementation.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint 1 and Backend Developer attempts to configure Azure AD app registration and discovers tenant policies block required OAuth scopes or require additional security approvals
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 begins, coordinate with Azure AD administrator to review tenant configuration, group policies, and security settings; confirm OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect is enabled and required scopes are available; obtain pre-approval for any security policy changes needed for SSO integration; document Azure AD configuration in Phase 1
risk_register.contingency: If Azure AD policies block SSO integration, escalate to Azure AD administrator and security team for policy exception or change request; implement alternative authentication method (e.g., username/password with MFA) as interim solution; defer advanced SSO features (e.g., conditional access, device compliance) to post-launch

risk_register.description: If Phase 1 requirements clarification (open questions Q1–Q6) extends beyond week 2, then Phase 2 kickoff will slip, compressing Phase 2 development window and risking Phase 3 testing and June 30 deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 1 week 2 and stakeholders have not provided written answers to open questions Q1 (SOC 2 scope), Q2 (e-signature vendor), Q3 (Product Owner), Q4 (data retention), Q5 (Workday API), Q6 (IT account scope)
risk_register.mitigation: Assign ownership of each open question to specific stakeholder in Phase 1 kickoff; set hard deadline of Phase 1 week 2 for written answers; schedule stakeholder review meeting in Phase 1 week 1 to discuss questions and set expectations; escalate unanswered questions to project sponsor by Phase 1 week 2 end
risk_register.contingency: If stakeholders cannot answer questions by Phase 1 week 2, proceed with Phase 2 kickoff using documented assumptions (A1–A5) and defer clarification to Phase 2 sprint 1; flag assumptions as high-risk and plan for scope adjustment if assumptions are invalidated

risk_register.description: If scope creep occurs from nice-to-have features (chat with HR bot, mobile app, LMS integration) being prioritized as must-haves, then Phase 2–3 development will consume additional budget and time, risking June 30 deadline and $80,000 budget.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint planning and stakeholders request that nice-to-have features (chat bot, mobile app, LMS integration) be included in MVP scope
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 begins, establish clear change control process and document nice-to-have features as post-launch backlog; require written change request and sponsor approval for any scope additions; track scope changes and budget impact in project dashboard; communicate MVP scope clearly to all stakeholders in Phase 1 kickoff
risk_register.contingency: If scope creep occurs during Phase 2, evaluate impact on schedule and budget; defer nice-to-have features to post-launch release; use feature flags to enable/disable features at launch; escalate scope change to project sponsor for approval and budget adjustment

risk_register.description: If performance requirements for portal (page load time, form submission latency, dashboard query performance) are not defined, then Phase 3 testing may reveal performance issues that require Phase 2 rework, consuming contingency and risking launch deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 3 performance testing and portal page load time exceeds acceptable threshold (e.g., >3 seconds) or dashboard queries timeout under expected load
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 begins, define performance requirements (page load time, form submission latency, dashboard query performance, concurrent user capacity); document in non-functional requirements; implement performance monitoring and load testing in Phase 2 to validate requirements early; establish performance baselines in Phase 2 sprint 1
risk_register.contingency: If Phase 3 testing reveals performance issues, implement caching (Redis), database query optimization, and frontend code splitting in Phase 3; defer advanced performance features (e.g., real-time notifications, advanced analytics) to post-launch

risk_register.description: If audit logging and data access controls required for SOC 2 compliance are not implemented in Phase 2, then Phase 3 will require rework to add compliance features, consuming contingency and risking launch deadline.
risk_register.trigger: Phase 2 sprint 2 and Backend Developer has not implemented audit logging for document uploads, data access, and user actions required for SOC 2 compliance
risk_register.mitigation: Before Phase 2 begins, define SOC 2 compliance requirements (audit logging, data access controls, encryption, access management); document in non-functional requirements; allocate Phase 2 sprint 1 to implement audit logging framework and data access controls; validate compliance implementation in Phase 2 sprint 2 before Phase 3 begins
risk_register.contingency: If compliance features are incomplete in Phase 2, allocate Phase 3 sprint 1 to complete audit logging and access controls; engage SOC 2 auditor in Phase 3 sprint 1 to identify gaps and remediation; defer advanced compliance features (e.g., encryption key rotation, compliance reporting) to post-launch

open_questions.question: Is SOC 2 Type II audit required before June 30, 2026 launch, or is Type I compliance at launch with Type II post-launch acceptable?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If Type II audit is pre-launch, Phase 3 requires 4-8 weeks of audit preparation and evidence collection, pushing launch past deadline. If post-launch, Phase 3 focuses on functional testing. Staffing and schedule depend on this clarification.

open_questions.question: Has e-signature service vendor (DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or equivalent) been selected and contracted? If not, who owns vendor selection in Phase 1?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If vendor is not selected by Phase 1 week 2, procurement will consume 2-3 weeks, compressing Phase 2 development window and delaying UC2 (Submit Required Documents) implementation.

open_questions.question: Who is the dedicated Product Owner responsible for backlog prioritization, sprint planning, and stakeholder feedback during Phase 2-3 sprints? Is PO allocated ≥50% to this project?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Hybrid SDLC requires a dedicated PO. Without clear PO assignment and allocation, sprint planning will stall and stakeholder feedback loops will be delayed, compressing Phase 3 testing.

open_questions.question: What is the definition of 'IT account setup automated'? Does this include email only, or email + Slack + SaaS tools (which ones)?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: Scope of IT account provisioning affects Phase 2 integration complexity (T15 effort estimate). Unclear scope may result in feature creep or incomplete automation at launch.

open_questions.question: Is Workday API sandbox environment, documentation, and SLA confirmed available? Does integration require custom Workday development or extended vendor support?
open_questions.impact_if_unanswered: If Workday API is unavailable, undocumented, or requires custom development, Phase 2 integration work (T13, T15) will slip 2-4 weeks, compressing Phase 3 testing and risking June 30 deadline.

consistency_issues.detail: Actor 'New Hire' (A1) mapped to Frontend Developer, UX Designer, QA Engineer — but A1 is a primary actor in use cases UC1, UC2, UC3, UC7, UC8. These are user-facing roles, not actor roles. Actor A1 should map to a business/system role (e.g., 'Portal User', 'New Hire User'). Current mapping conflates actor with development team roles.

Actor 'HR Administrator' (A2) mapped to Product Manager, Frontend Developer, QA Engineer — but A2 is a primary actor in use case UC5 (Monitor Onboarding Progress). A2 should map to a business role (e.g., 'HR Admin User'), not development team roles.

Actor 'IT Administrator' (A3) mapped to Backend Developer, QA Engineer — but A3 is a primary actor in use case UC4 (Provision IT Accounts). A3 should map to a business role (e.g., 'IT Admin User'), not development team roles.
